handoff.summary: Extended gate-green salvage so an optional P2 cleanup that is refused before DEV runs due to allocation exhaustion lands the previously recorded gate-green, review-approved checkpoint instead of failing the story. The engine now routes pre-DEV cleanup refusals through the existing salvage helper, and the helper recognizes allocation-exhausted P2-cleanup escalations, including the case where HEAD already equals the checkpoint because the cleanup attempt never ran.

commits.message: fix(coordinator): salvage checkpoint on cleanup refusal

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A story refused dev funding for cleanup after a gate-green/review-approved checkpoint was recorded must land at the checkpoint (pending_integration) rather than fail, with outstanding P2s returned to backlog.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Pre-DEV cleanup refusals now pass through gate_green_salvage and convert to DONE/pending_integration when a checkpoint exists; tests cover helper-level and run_from_review seam behavior.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A story with no gate-green checkpoint recorded must continue to fail exactly as before.
acceptance_criteria.notes: The salvage helper still returns the original ESCALATE result when no checkpoint exists; added cleanup-refusal no-checkpoint coverage to pin that behavior.

reviews.summary: [openai-gpt-5.5-cli] The change routes allocation-exhausted optional cleanup refusals through the existing gate-green salvage path and covers the observed runtime shape with targeted tests. | [anthropic-opus-cli] Pre-DEV cleanup funding refusals now route through gate_green_salvage and land the recorded floor; helper- and seam-level tests reproduce the issue-1918 shape and the no-checkpoint path still fails unchanged (33 salvage tests + 171 budget/rca tests pass locally at the reviewed HEAD, which matches the authoritative PASS commit).

findings.description: A story whose optional cleanup was refused for funding is salvaged to DONE with landing_status pending_integration, but state.error_type is left as allocation_exhausted (only state.error is cleared), so the sprint story row records outcome_code=allocation_exhausted and the allocation block records status=allocation_exhausted for a story that actually landed.

Only the non-review funding refusal is routed through the salvage helper; other ways an optional post-APPROVE cleanup iteration can end without producing anything — a dev-phase escalation such as a timeout or an agent startup failure during the P2 cleanup iteration — still return their escalation directly and discard the gate-green, review-approved checkpoint recorded moments earlier.

ac_verification.criterion: Symptom resolution: A story that reaches review approval, records a gate-green checkpoint, and then has optional P2 cleanup refused before DEV runs must land the checkpoint instead of failing and must not change no-checkpoint failures.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
